hook.line: I'm going to show you how to get bestseller SEO on all your Etsy listings.
hook.visual: A phone filming a laptop showing Etsy search results for Valentine's gifts, with a white title box 'How to have BESTSELLER SEO on Etsy' mid-frame.

beats.what: Etsy search results filmed off a laptop screen with the white title box in the middle
Close-up of the 'Show filters' button being clicked
URL highlighted; 'star_seller' is about to be swapped for 'best'
Zoom punch on the edited URL reading is_best_seller=true
A similar listing opened with a Bestseller badge and sales stats panel
Finger points at the 'Analyze listing' button of the extension
Sales chart and keyword table with volume and competition
Competitor tags pasted into her own listing's tag field and pruned
Thumbs-up to camera with 'Make sure to save this and follow for more Etsy tips!'

why_it_works: The promise is a concrete, repeatable hack (edit one word in the URL), so viewers save it to try later; shares are high for the play count
Every step is a close jump cut on the exact button or URL being changed, with a zoom punch on the key edit, so nothing has to be explained twice
The product (the listing-analysis extension) is woven in as one step of the tutorial, so the ad never feels like an ad
Filming the screen with a phone, finger and keyboard visible, reads as a real person doing it, not a polished promo
weaknesses: No face and no spoken energy; the hook relies on the title box alone
Small on-screen UI text is hard to read on a phone, and most of it sits outside the safe area
No captions for the narration, so muted viewers lose the steps
for_robert: Use the zoom punch on the single changed detail (here the one word in a URL): when Robert explains a GEO/SEO trick, cut to the exact screen spot and punch in, with Fred pointing at it, instead of showing the whole page.
